title: Simulated velocity tests of three TOI-682 states depend on planet masses and free periodic terms
abstract: We test 24 simulated radial velocities at 2 m/s precision over six months in 2027 for three published TOI-682 orbit states. For a two-planet truth, a three-planet fit attains joint chi-square 112.21 with fixed source masses, but 23.76 when four periodic velocity terms are free. The latter fit has past timing-plus-shape chi-square 19.30 and RV residual 0.86 m/s. A consistent gravitational fit with two free positive masses reaches chi-square 38.70 and residual 1.79 m/s, but reduces the reported 16.134-day companion minimum mass to 0.72 Earth masses from the fixed 9.6. The two-planet own-family fit reaches chi-square 20.55. Most searches reach an evaluation limit, so their large losses are not exclusions. These tests add no observations or mass estimates. They show that forecasts based on fixed RV components can overstate model separation. We preserve input states, dates, local design scores, numerical checks, final endpoints and code. The extra velocity terms are a sensitivity test, not a gravitational or stellar-activity model. Agreement with the actual RV data, noise assumptions and long-term survival remain untested.

display.caption: Three stellar velocity predictions and local visit scores. Free periodic velocity terms greatly reduce some scores; see nonlinear and physical-bound checks.

Attained joint losses with two-planet simulated truth. Free velocity terms or masses reduce the loss. These are limited searches, not global exclusions or evidence that the original RV data allow the fitted changes.
